$comment: The cel texture style (docs/PAINTERLY_TEXTURES.md §10): a prototype second atlas for the pixel-art preview (docs/proposals/PIXEL_ART_LOOK.md), chosen by a preset's `textures`; the normal look keeps the painterly set. Each material of materials.json is painted by shared/textures/cel.mjs on a tileTexels × tileTexels grid (one tile per metre, as the atlas lays tiles out), in a few flat tones with hard edges and large flat areas, so a face holds still in motion. A material's recipe is recipes.<material>, else the recipe of the material it is `like`, else defaults.<use>. Layers paint in order; a tone is a palette reference (shared/textures/palette.json: "ramp.stop", "@stop" for the material's own ramp, a swatch) or "clear" (a cutout's gap). Kinds: fill {tone}; edge {tone, edge, width, ragged}; clumps {tone, count, width, height, band, shape rect|blob, light, shadow}; blades {tone, tip, count | at, length, width, root, dir up|down}; bricks {mortar, width, height, light, shadow}; planks {seam, direction, width, light, joints}; bands {tones, direction, width}; ripples {tone, under, count, length, band}; rings {tones, center, step, metric round|square, radius}; rects {tone, at [[x, y, w, h]]}; checker {tone, size}; any layer: clip (paint only covered texels), seed. Sizes are whole texels, y up. mips: how the atlas halves the opaque tiles for their mip levels, 'average' or 'mode' (each 2 × 2 to its majority tone, so a distant face keeps the tile's tones and settles on its main one instead of averaging into colours the palette dithers). Every tile has at most maxTones colours, and every tile but paletteExempt (the utility tiles, not content) paints only colours of the pixel-art palette `palette` (shared/look/pixelart.json), so quantizing a lit-white face changes nothing. Run `node shared/textures/gen.mjs` after editing; CI fails if crates/dwell-mesh/src/cel.rgba is stale.

block.$comment: A block material with no recipe: its base with a few blocky clumps of shadow and a lit top row.

character.$comment: Characters (docs/CHARACTERS.md): flat base, a shadow band along the bottom and a lit rim along the top — three tones; parts read by their shape, not their texture.

grass_top.$comment: Turf from above: mostly flat base, three big blocky shadow clumps and a few small lit tufts (few, large shapes: less to crawl in motion).

grass_side.$comment: Soil with a hanging skirt of turf (the material hangs: a ½ m block shows the tile's top half): a ragged band of meadow with drips, a lit rim, over plain soil.

stone.$comment: Big rough-cut blocks, about two a tile each way: shadow mortar outlines, a lit top row on each stone, flat stone between.

sand.$comment: Flat sand with a few wind ripples: a lit dash with its shadow under.

bark.$comment: Wood grain as vertical bands: wide base, narrow shadow furrows, a rare lit ridge.

log_end.$comment: A cut log: growth rings in two tones and a rim of bark.

leaves.$comment: Blocky leaf clusters with gaps (a cutout): each cluster lit along its top row and shaded along its bottom.

tall_grass.$comment: A sprite on crossed quads: blades rooted on the bottom row, clear of the side columns and the top row, lit at the tips.

ladder_wood.$comment: Two rails and four rungs (a cutout), each rung shaded along its bottom; the rungs on even rows, so each mip halves them whole, and rails wider than the rungs, so the smallest mips don't go all or nothing (the coverage test).

torch.$comment: The torch's lower cell: a plain two-texel stick, lit on its left.

torch_top.$comment: The torch's upper cell: the stick's top, its tip at 0.1 m (its flame is the flame effect).
